title: Canada's population estimates, second quarter 2026
key_claim: Canada's population was 41,798,407 on 1 July 2026 with 2,779,774 non-permanent residents; updated estimates were issued for every quarter from the third quarter of 2021 to the first quarter of 2026, and the 2026 Census counts follow on 10 February 2027. Analyst note: the stock is about 2.8 million; the 2.5 million figure used as a disconfirming threshold is an analyst threshold, not a source figure.
frame_summary: Reports the official quarterly population estimate as preliminary and updated back to 2021, and separates it from the 2026 Census counts due in February 2027.

title: Canada: Data Revisions Complicate the Path to the Federal Population Target
key_claim: Revised data show non-permanent residents fell about 185,000 between Q4 2024 and Q1 2026, not 591,000, so about 905,000 departures are needed by the end of next year to reach the 5% target. Analyst arithmetic: spread over the six quarters from 1 July 2026 to the end of 2027, that is above 150,000 a quarter.
frame_summary: Argues that the revisions make the federal 5% non-permanent resident target harder to reach and may require faster declines in coming quarters.
verbatim_quote: NPRs would need to fall by roughly 905k by the end of next year from their most recent level.
verbatim_list: As a result, NPRs fell by roughly 185k between Q4 2024 and Q1 2026, rather than 591k under the previous population numbers.
The share fell to 6.7% as of July 1 of this year from its peak of 7.2% on October 1, 2024.
